what_happened: The job "Classify PR commits by content in pr_commits, not Athena-Job trailers" (20261024-153908-1rve) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic judged the plan mostly sound and grounded in the code. The symbols it names exist, and the operator/ governance analysis is right. The plan removes the trailers instead of adding exceptions, and its demonstrations would fail without the new behaviour. One major finding remained. Decision 3 requires the candidate, verification and outcome files to be added in the same commit. That would refuse a real blocked-then-retried landing, which adds only outcome-landed.json (run.rs retry_landing), even though the gate accepts that shape. This contradicts the goal that real PRs stop being refused. There was one minor finding: the realistic-range test passes only because its fixture adds an operator/ exclusion this repo does not have. There was one nit: the plan runs `cargo test -p athena-gate invariant`, which goes beyond the brief's "only athena-core land and gh tests". The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planning stage derives a commit-shape rule from the intended happy path instead of from the full set of shapes the system produces. Here it missed the retry-after-block landing. The plan's demonstrations also use a fixture that does not match this repo's real history, so the tests pass while the rule is wrong. Nothing in the plan template makes the planner list every real commit shape the rule must accept and refuse, and tie each to its writer (such as retry_landing) and to a fixture matching the repo. The critic finds this only by reading code, so it surfaces late. The three-round cap has no fallback: major findings are not required to shrink, no partial plan is kept, and a retry starts without the critic's findings. The same feature already failed once with a bare producer timeout (20261024-145615-7s8b), and the retry has no memory of that.
prevention: Change the plan template and critic checklist for any landing or history-check rule. The plan must include an enumerated table of every commit shape the real branch contains. The table must cover job commits, records-only commits, owner-path commits, intervention commits, blocked-then-retried landings that add only outcome-landed.json, and stacked landings. Each row names the code that writes the shape and says whether the rule accepts or refuses it. Each row needs a test run on a fixture built from this repo's actual governance settings, with no added exclusions. Add a mechanical check that every writer of landing records (such as retry_landing) appears in the table. Also pass the previous attempt's critic findings into the retry, and require major findings to shrink across rounds. Under that design Decision 3 would have been written as "adds a landed outcome; candidate and verification are present in the tree".
proposed_request: Classify the commits in a pull request by what they change, not by Athena-Job trailers, in pr_commits (athena-core land). Outcome: real pull requests that Athena lands are no longer refused for missing trailers. This covers job commits, records-only commits, owner-path commits, intervention commits, and a blocked job that is later landed by a commit adding only outcome-landed.json. Rules: (1) a job landing is recognised when the commit adds a landed outcome and the candidate and verification files are already present in the tree, whether added in the same commit or an earlier one; (2) remove the trailer dependence instead of adding exceptions; (3) keep operator/ governed as this repo configures it. Acceptance: tests cover each commit shape above, including the retry_landing shape. They run against a fixture that matches this repo's real governance settings, with no extra operator/ exclusion. Run only the athena-core land and gh tests. Before planning, list every writer of landing records in the code and make sure each is covered. Note that a previous attempt at this change (20261024-140624-ewbs) timed out in the producer, and a planning attempt (20261024-153908-1rve) failed on the rule that all three landing files must be added in one commit.
